Then $F_{\mathrm{rem},\lambda}(\Phi,W)=F_{\mathrm{rem}}(\Phi,W)$ coefficientwise, while the gauge-kinetic coefficient vector $\boldsymbol\tau_\lambda$ may receive one-loop corrections but no higher-loop corrections. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Use the mostly-plus metric and the matrices $\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}$ specified by the four-dimensional super-Poincare algebra. A **chiral superfield** is an even element $\Phi\in\mathscr S$ satisfying the two equations

$$\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi=0,\qquad \bar D_{\dot\alpha}:=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}-i\sum_{\alpha,\mu}\theta^\alpha\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu,\quad \dot\alpha\in\{\dot1,\dot2\}.$$

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, flat spacetime $\mathcal M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, coordinates $x^0=ct$, and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. $$\mathcal L_\lambda=[\sum_i\Phi_i^\dagger e^{-V_i}\Phi_i+G_\lambda]_D+2\operatorname{Re}[\frac{\tau_\lambda}{8\pi i}\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm h}(W^\alpha W_\alpha)+F_\lambda(\Phi,W)]_F,$$

where the physical action brackets are $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$, $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from Physical superspace action brackets and canonical chiral components, with physical chiral components $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$. $$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{\Delta_\alpha\le D_{\max}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{L_{\max}}\zeta^\ell C_{\alpha,\ell}(\mu_W)\frac{\mathcal O_\alpha}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{\Delta_\alpha-4}},$$

In the same natural-unit convention, $D_\alpha$, $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$, $Q_\alpha$ and $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha}$ have mass dimension $+\tfrac12$, while $[\epsilon^\alpha]=[\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}]=-\tfrac12$, so $\delta_{\epsilon,\bar\epsilon}$ is dimensionless.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
